BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Most of its positions are at or beyond our fallback limits, and several would strip protection from the categories we must keep separate (Title, Fundamental, Tax, IP, Fraud). Nothing in the package is agreed. The Seller's statement that the positions were "settled at principal level" and "FINAL" is not supported by any authority in our file. Amelia Frost has given no written approval of any fallback, so none of these terms can be accepted on her behalf.

## 1. Departures from playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m. 20% is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None given. | Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000 aggregate, then liable from the first dollar (tipping) | Reject. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping. |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval. None given. | Reject. Counter at 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims" | Blanket override across all claim types | No hidden general-regime override | Reject. Delete. |
| Fundamental/Title (cl 12) | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable | Reject. Insert the fraud carve-out. |
| Disclosure (cl 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public searches | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew or could find in the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject. Delete. |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are met before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Make it a condition precedent with evidence. |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7) | Release provided after Completion | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. Require payout at Completion. |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005, funds flow) | "A matter for the Seller." Not in funds flow | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or Seller-funded. Funds flow must not silently exclude them | Reject. Itemise and Seller-fund. |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity. Preserve the SOW3 cure. AUD 180,000 unverified either way | Reject. Broaden. |
| Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6, Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand | Do not accept "immaterial". Do not assert breach either. |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic debt classification or price deduction | Do not accept the label. Request contracts and terms. |
| Tax/IP (cl summary) | "Settled under the general regime" | Tax and IP terms remain open. No unlimited liability assumed, no resolution | Reject. Keep Tax and IP separate. |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences 100% title | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Require independent evidence (see below). |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

### 2.1 Limitation structure: the seller's terms compound

The caps, thresholds and time limits operate together, so the combined effect matters more than any single number.

- **Basket and de minimis.** Under the Seller's draft, a AUD 200,000 general claim recovers nothing because it does not exceed the AUD 250,000 basket. Under our playbook, it recovers the full AUD 200,000 once the AUD 50,000 basket is exceeded. A AUD 300,000 claim recovers only AUD 50,000 under the Seller's draft and the full AUD 300,000 under ours.
- **Cap and time.** The Seller's cap is AUD 1.2m lower, and claims discovered in months 19 to 24 are barred.
- **Buyer knowledge and disclosure.** Clause 8.3 and the data-room disclosure both operate on the same facts. Combined, they exclude any claim on a matter that was in the data room, which covers most of the issues the Seller has already disclosed (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-005, DD-006, DD-008). Our known issues would then have no recourse under the general warranties. This is why specific indemnities and conditions are necessary for each known issue.
- **Fundamental claims.** Subjecting title and capacity to the general regime would leave title defects capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window. That is the most serious structural problem in the package.

### 2.2 Fraud carve-out

The Seller's limitation and exclusive-remedy language reaches "all Claims of any nature" with no fraud exception. Our playbook requires the carve-out to the maximum extent enforceable and states that no one may waive it. This must be inserted expressly. Without it, a deliberate concealment of the export incident or the Riverlark position could be argued to fall under the cap.

### 2.3 Specific disclosed issues

**Bluefen (about 30% of FY26 revenue, AUD 3.6m).** The Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent and no evidence that conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. The Seller's "consent-on-delivery" and reasonable-endeavours language would let Completion occur without an effective consent. Given the revenue concentration, this is a condition precedent requirement, not a commercial item.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding).** The Seller's draft defers the release until after Completion. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. This is a debt-free/cash-free issue. Payment should come from Completion funds. Without this, Wattlebridge takes the company subject to a secured facility. We also need a current payout letter and PPSR evidence that security will be released.

**Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).** The funds flow omits the bonuses and the disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation apply. If the bonuses crystallise in the company after Completion, the cost falls on Wattlebridge. They must be itemised in the funds flow or funded by the Seller. We should also require a payroll tax and superannuation position, which the Seller has not provided.

**Ironquay (AUD 180,000 open).** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 project materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. A narrow payment indemnity would not cover a failed IP transfer, a dispute over materials, or other SOW fees. We broaden the indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not verified, and we should not treat it as either paid or unpaid without evidence.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006, about 1,240 records).** Both sides agree the investigation is preliminary. The Seller calls the matter "not expected to be material", which we should not accept without a completed investigation. Our position is neutral: preserve logs, require investigation scope and timing, and require regular updates. Whether notification is required under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme is a question for privacy counsel. We should not assert or deny a breach at this stage. The playbook does not specify an indemnity for this matter. Whether to seek one is a deal-team decision.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000).** The Disclosure Letter says the three renewals should be read together for timing and scope, and does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Each is AUD 110,000, above the proposed de minimis, so aggregation is not a concern for the threshold. We should request the contracts, notice periods and any prepayments. The playbook prohibits automatic debt treatment or price deduction, so the renewals should be assessed rather than deducted.

**Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Disclosure Letter says neither clause, as described, requires consent merely because the shares are sold. The playbook does not address these directly. We should still request landlord and Mossvale confirmation as part of ordinary diligence, and keep them separate from the general regime.

### 2.4 Title evidence

The Seller relies on the company share register at DD-012. The playbook treats this as an internal supplied source, not independent proof. Before Completion we should require:

- An ASIC company extract and current register of members
- Signed share transfer forms and evidence of stamping, where required
- Evidence of authority for the Seller signatories
- PPSR and encumbrance searches on the shares and company assets
- Confirmation that no options, pre-emption rights or other interests affect the shares

### 2.5 Tax and IP

The Seller says tax and IP are "settled under the general regime". That is incorrect under our playbook. Tax and IP warranties remain open, and we should not assume unlimited liability or any resolution. We should insist that Tax and IP are separate categories, not subject to the general cap, basket or time limit.

### 2.6 "Final" and market-standard claims

The Seller's market commentary (10 to 20% caps, baskets around 1%, 12 to 18 month periods) is its characterisation, not a standard we have adopted. Our playbook governs. The Seller's statement that positions are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened" does not bind us, because no principal-level approval from Amelia Frost exists on file. We should say so expressly in our response.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as drafted.** Respond that the Seller's positions are not agreed and that the Buyer's playbook governs.
2. **Counter the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket; 24-month period. Do not offer the 20%, 18-month or other fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Insert the fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
5. **Delete the general disclosure** (cl 1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) and require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar** (cl 8.3). Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
8. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
9. **Employee bonuses:** itemise AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs in the funds flow, or require Seller funding. Request payroll tax and superannuation confirmation.
10. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify the AUD 180,000 position.
11. **Export/privacy incident:** require log preservation, investigation scope and timing, and regular updates. Refer notification analysis to privacy counsel. Do not characterise the matter either way.
12. **Sandbar renewals:** request contracts and terms. Assess, do not deduct.
13. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as the Seller's source only.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate. Reject the "settled under general regime" statement.
15. **Lease and Mossvale:** request confirmation that no consent is required on the share sale.

**Next steps:** Obtain Amelia Frost's instructions on any fallback we might consider. Confirm the responsible NSW lawyer has reviewed the response. Engage privacy and tax specialists for the DD-006 and bonus on-cost questions.
